[How rights work](/operate/how-rights-work/) explains the same system in full detail. ## Two questions **Who are you?** A person who signs in. A person who is a member of a workspace also gets what is shared there. A Workflow runs as a technical account that it names; a Superadmin creates that account on the API access page. An agent has none: it acts with the rights of the person it works for, and a tool on an agent adds no right. **What may you do?** A right is an action in a place, for example "use the Connection DATEV". The place is one workspace, one item, or the whole instance. A role bundles rights; the three roles User, Admin and Superadmin are fixed. A right is given to a person, to a Workflow's technical account, or comes with a role. Three rules always hold: - Nothing is allowed until it is given. - A deny beats every allow, even an administrator's. Exporting an agent and setting the default agent are not affected. - Using is not editing. Whoever may open an App may not change it for that reason. ## Where an App gets its data, and who sees it An App shows data in two ways: live from an outside system, or from its Data Store. A Data Store is filled by Workflows, by the App's own actions that add rows, and by people with the right to add rows. The two ways follow different rules. The numbers in the picture are the four decisions on the way. 1. **Catalyst decides who may reach the outside system.** The App calls the Connection as Anna. Anna needs the right to use the Connection herself; the App lends her none. The operation must also list Apps under **Callable by** ("Aufrufbar durch"). 2. **The outside system decides what it shows.** It answers with what the account the Connection signed in with may see there. 3. **The Workflow runs as its technical account,** whether a person or a schedule starts it. It can do only what that account may. Whoever publishes it decides what gets copied. A test run of a draft is different: it acts as the person testing, and can do only what both that person and the Workflow's account may. 4. **Whoever may open the App sees what its queries show.** For an App in a workspace, these are the workspace's members, and the instance's administrators. So two rules apply: - **Read live:** the rights of the person looking count. - **Stored:** like an exported report, the App is the gate. Whoever may open it sees what its queries show, without a right on the Connection. The person who publishes the App needs the right to read the Data Store where the App reads from it, and the right to add rows where the App adds rows. ## Workspaces A workspace is where a team works together. Members see its shared conversations, open its Apps and use the agents offered there. Private conversations stay private. Being a member is not building. Editing a workspace's agents and skills is a right of its own, given on the Access page. Someone who only builds need not be a member and sees no conversations. A workspace's Apps are edited by administrators. An agent of the whole instance can be offered in several workspaces under **Available in** ("Verfügbar in"). Only someone with the right to edit agents on the whole instance can change where it is offered. ## Connections A Connection is signed in with one shared account ("Ein gemeinsames Konto"). Everyone who may use it sees the same in the outside system: what that account sees. If a team should be able to do less, create a second Connection with fewer operations and give the right to use it to each person of that team. A right on a Connection is given on that one Connection. Writing, deleting and approving Connections stay with the Admin role. ## Not built yet - **Groups and custom roles.** A right names one person or one technical account. - **Personal Connections**, where each person signs in with their own account. - **Rows per person.** An App's query cannot yet limit itself to the rows of the person looking. - **Namespaces** still appear on the Access page. They are being retired; the workspace takes over their job. [Rights for one person or asset](/operate/rights-and-namespaces/) describes them.

pages.title: Guardrails
pages.description: Rules that check an action just before it happens and warn, ask for an approval or block; how to read them in Studio, and how to write, test and publish one.
pages.body:
A guardrail is a rule that checks an action just before it happens, for example "no bank account numbers in skills". When the rule matches, the guardrail warns, sends the action for approval, or blocks it.

The German interface shows the labels in quotes.

## When a guardrail runs

A guardrail is bound to one moment:

- before an asset is saved, such as an agent, a skill or an App draft, whether in Studio, by an agent or with the CLI;
- before any operation is called, by a person, an agent, an App or a Workflow;
- before an App, a Workflow or a Data Store is published;
- before a request for approval is filed, such as a skill change an agent proposes.

It can be narrowed further, for example to skills only, to one agent, or to one workspace.

Studio says this in one sentence for each guardrail, under **When it runs** ("Wann sie greift"). For example:

> Runs before an agent saves a skill, in workspace Finance. Checks the content for a text pattern. Blocks if the check fails.

> Läuft, bevor ein Agent einen Skill speichert, im Workspace Finance. Prüft den Inhalt auf ein Textmuster. Blockiert, wenn die Prüfung anschlägt.

## What happens when one matches

| On a hit ("Bei einem Treffer") | What the person sees |
| --- | --- |
| **Warns** ("Warnt") | The action goes ahead. The reason is shown and kept beside it. |
| **Needs approval** ("Braucht Freigabe") | A change waits in the **Inbox** ("Eingang") until someone who may decide approves it. A read can't wait, so it is refused; so is a change that can't wait, such as an agent saving into an App draft. |
| **Blocks** ("Blockiert") | Nothing happens. The person or the agent is told the guardrail's reason. |

When a guardrail blocks something an agent tried in a chat, the agent's step shows as failed, such as "Could not change …", "Could not read …" or "The save failed", followed by the guardrail's reason, or "A guardrail blocked the call" when it gives none.

Every guardrail that applies runs, and the strictest answer wins. A guardrail can only make things stricter: it never allows what a right or the policy refuses.

A guardrail checks either for a **text pattern** ("Muster"), such as the shape of an IBAN, or with a **model** that reads the content against a written rule. A model check is a model call of the instance and counts toward its usage.

## Read them in Studio

Open **Studio** and choose **Guardrails** ("Leitplanken"). Each row has the sentence that says when it runs, and what it does on a hit. Open one to see:

- **Check** ("Prüfung"): when it runs, what it applies to ("Gilt für"), how it checks ("Wie sie prüft") and what it does on a hit;
- **Recent hits** ("Letzte Treffer"): how often it warned, held or blocked in the last 7 and 30 days, and the newest hits.

Hits never name a person. They say which rule, when, and what kind of thing was checked, not who did it. A list of who tripped which rule would make the instance a tool for watching employees.

The page in Studio only reads. You write a guardrail with the CLI, as below.

## Where guardrails come from

- **The operator's floor.** The operator sets guardrails in the release config. They always run, nobody can change or stop them in the product, and Studio marks them "set by the operator".
- **Guardrails written as assets.** An administrator writes further guardrails for the whole instance or for one shared workspace. They add checks to the floor and never remove one. A workspace's guardrail checks only what happens in that workspace.

Only the operator's guardrails check changes to guardrails, so a guardrail can never stop you from fixing one.

## Write, try and publish a guardrail

You write a guardrail as a file and save it with [the CLI](/configure/cli/): `catalyst guardrail put <name> --from <folder> --if-revision new`, or `catalyst config push` from a working copy. [Guardrails as assets](/configure/config-assets/#guardrails-as-assets) shows the file. A new guardrail is a **draft**: it checks nothing until it is published.

1. **Try it on an example.** `catalyst guardrail test <name> --text "<sample>"` says what the draft would answer. `--asset skill:<name>` tries it on an existing skill. A test keeps no hit.
2. **See what it would have done.** `catalyst guardrail dry-run <name>` counts what the draft would have warned on, held or blocked in the last 14 days, without names.
3. **Publish it.** `catalyst guardrail publish <name> --revision <n>` shows the dry run first. If the guardrail would have stopped actions, it asks you to confirm with the number it counted (`--confirm <n>`). Tip: publish it with the outcome "warn" first and watch its hits for a while.
4. **Stop it** with `catalyst guardrail unpublish <name>`. The draft stays.

Publishing is a right of its own. Administrators hold it for the instance. To let someone set the rules of one shared workspace, an administrator opens **Settings > Instance > Access** ("Einstellungen › Instanz › Zugriff"), clicks **New right** ("Neues Recht") and chooses **Publish guardrails** for that workspace: "Make a guardrail of this workspace enforce, or stop it. A guardrail stops other people's work in the workspace."

## More detail

- [Guardrails as assets](/configure/config-assets/#guardrails-as-assets): the file format and the rules for workspace guardrails.
- [Release config, Guardrails](/configure/release-config/#guardrails): the floor, every field, and how content and files are read.
- [How rights work](/operate/how-rights-work/#guardrails): where guardrails sit among rights and policy.

pages.title: Sign-in and embedding
pages.description: Connect Workshape Catalyst to users in an existing customer application.
pages.body:
The embedded chat path should rely on the customer application as the login authority.

Workshape Catalyst receives a short-lived chat session token and maps it into a product-owned authenticated user.

## Recommended Embedded Flow

```text
authenticated customer app session
  -> widget asks customer backend for a chat session token
  -> customer backend verifies its own user
  -> customer backend calls chat backend token endpoint
  -> chat backend returns short-lived chat session token
  -> widget calls chat API with that token
```

The browser never receives the customer app's server-to-server credential.

## Browser Origins

Configure each embedding site's exact origin through the client assembly's `allowedOrigins`,
`CHAT_UI_ORIGIN`, or `auth.standalone.trustedOrigins`. The assembly merges these into one list
for Better Auth, CORS, and session-cookie origin checks. Development expands configured
loopback origins to `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, and `[::1]` at the same port. Without configured
origins, same-origin requests still work; cross-origin requests receive no CORS grant.

Both the assembly and direct `createChatServer` callers accept `allowedOrigins` as a string
or an array of strings. Startup validates HTTP and HTTPS URLs, serializes their origins,
and removes duplicates. Wildcards, opaque origins, and other value types are rejected.

Cookie-authenticated writes require an allowed or same-server `Origin`. When `Origin` is
absent, only `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin` is accepted. GET, HEAD, and OPTIONS are exempt.
Bearer tokens, API-key exchange, and server credentials do not require this cookie check,
but browser callers still need their origin configured for CORS. Custom cookie auth adapters
must return `authenticationMethod: "session-cookie"` on the authenticated user.

An `Authorization` or `X-Server-Credential` header excludes standalone cookie and development
authentication, regardless of adapter order. Invalid explicit credentials never fall back to
a standalone session. Token-authenticated requests do not use the cookie origin check.
The cookie-only `/api/auth/*` endpoints, including session lookup and sign-out, reject
requests carrying either explicit credential header without accessing the session.

The API client omits cookies whenever `getToken` is configured, even if it currently returns
no token. Passing a widget `token` also selects this mode. Token-mode downloads and event
streams use the same transport; browser-managed downloads are disabled even if requested.
Without a token source, standalone requests, downloads, and event streams keep using cookies.
Every auth adapter must declare `credentialMode: "ambient"` or `"explicit"`. Only explicitly
marked credential adapters are consulted when an explicit credential header is present;
unmarked adapters are excluded too. Wrappers must preserve the wrapped adapter's mode.

## Token Claims

Keep token claims minimal:

- stable external user id
- display label
- optional verified email
- roles or permission refs
- client instance id
- expiry
- correlation id where useful

Do not put sensitive documents, tool outputs, long-lived credentials, or workflow payloads in the token.

## Identity Mapping

Conversation ownership should use a product-owned user identity.

External auth-source ids map to product users through user identity mappings. This allows standalone and embedded identities to share one conversation owner when linking is allowed and unambiguous.

Verified email can be a linking hint. It should not be the durable account key.

## Standalone And Control Plane Login

Standalone chat and control-plane routes may need their own login path.

The platform default is to keep that behind the same product-owned auth contract and use a self-hosted auth implementation internally. Do not expose auth-library user or session types across platform public boundaries.

## API Keys

An instance has two kinds of API keys. Both are exchanged at `POST /api/v1/auth/access-token` for a short-lived access token, and both need `SERVICE_ACCESS_TOKEN_SECRET` (below).

- **A personal key** acts as the person who issued it, narrowed to the scopes ticked when it was made, and never does more than that person may at the moment of a call. A person issues one under **Settings > You > API keys** (German: **Einstellungen › Du › API-Schlüssel**) or with `catalyst login`, which saves it for the CLI. A key lives at most a year, and no key issues another key. This needs the module `personalApiKeys`. See [Log in](/configure/cli/#log-in).
- **A service principal's key** is for automation such as CI or another system. It acts as the service principal and never as a person.

### Service Principals

Non-human clients are service principals, not product users. A service principal owns permissions and may have multiple independently revocable API keys. An API key is exchanged at `POST /api/v1/auth/access-token` for a short-lived service access token; normal API calls use that access token and do not create a product-user record.

Set a stable, high-entropy `SERVICE_ACCESS_TOKEN_SECRET` of at least 32 characters on the API server to enable exchange. It signs short-lived service tokens, must match across replicas, and must remain stable across restarts. API keys themselves live hashed in the database; their plaintext value is shown only once at creation and must be stored in an operator or CI secret store.

Keep machine credentials separate from embedded-chat credentials. `CHAT_SERVER_CREDENTIAL` authorizes a trusted customer backend to issue human chat session tokens at `POST /api/v1/instance/session-tokens` with the `x-server-credential` header; the CLI does not use it.

## Embed Surface

The embed surface should be small:

- load the chat shell
- request or receive a chat session token
- pass safe client config to the UI
- send chat requests to the dedicated chat backend

Customer application code should not need to know agent runtime, tool execution, or database internals.

pages.title: Capacity and limits
pages.description: Size an instance using the limits enforced by the platform code.
pages.body:
For an instance serving 5,000 to 10,000 people, size against simultaneous runs, model calls, uploaded files and retained conversations. The code states limits for individual requests and workers. It does not state a supported people count or a hardware size for that population.

The tables below describe the platform packages in this repository. A capability can add its own limits. Check its implementation separately, especially for document ingestion. Defaults are the values used when the setting is omitted. MiB means 1,048,576 bytes and KiB means 1,024 bytes. Source paths are relative to the repository root.

**Fixed** means there is no release config or environment knob. Where a TypeScript constructor option exists, the table names it separately. A page size bounds one response or screen, not the number of stored records. A renewable lease detects a lost worker; it is not a maximum job duration.

See [deployment](/operate/deployment/), [release config](/configure/release-config/) and [governance](/operate/governance/) for deployment and policy details.

## Chat and runs

Runtime defaults come from `packages/config-schema/src/schemas.ts`. The implementation is in `packages/agent-runtime/src/local-agent-runtime.ts`.

| What it bounds                                                  | Default                                             | Grows with                            | Knob and source                                                                                                                                                | What a person sees at the limit                                                                                                                                |
| --------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Model steps in one agent run                                    | 64                                                  | Runs and tool rounds                  | `runtime.maxSteps`; an agent's `maxSteps` overrides it. Runtime fallback: `DEFAULT_MAX_STEPS` in `local-agent-runtime.ts`.                                     | The run fails with “Agent exceeded the maximum step limit”.                                                                                                    |
| Identical calls to the same tool with the same input in one run | 3                                                   | Runs and repeated tool calls          | `runtime.repeatedToolCallLimit`; fallback `DEFAULT_REPEATED_TOOL_CALL_LIMIT` in `local-agent-runtime.ts`.                                                      | The fourth call returns a `repeated_tool_call` failure to the agent, which can continue with a different call.                                                 |
| Wait for the source of an agent's data tools, at the start of a run and at each call of one | 10 seconds | Runs of agents that list data tools | `runtime.dataToolDescribeTimeoutMs`; fallback `DATA_TOOL_DESCRIBE_TIMEOUT_MS` in `packages/agent-runtime/src/model-tool-materialization.ts` and `packages/tool-execution/src/tool-operation.ts`. When it is reached the run goes on without data tools, or the one call fails. |
| Recent history projected to a model without provider compaction | Target of 20 messages                               | Conversations and messages            | `DEFAULT_CONVERSATION_HISTORY_LIMIT` in `local-agent-runtime.ts`; TypeScript option `historyMessageLimit`, no release config knob.                             | Older context is omitted from the model request. Complete history groups are kept, so the result can exceed 20 messages. The stored conversation is unchanged. |
| Provider compaction threshold                                   | Unset                                               | Conversation context                  | `infrastructure.models.<id>.contextManagement.compaction.compactThresholdTokens` in `packages/config-schema/src/infrastructure.ts`; requires `api: responses`. | When configured, the provider compacts context at its threshold and the runtime keeps a continuation. This threshold does not cap stored messages.             |
| Text from each tool result projected to the model               | 60,000 estimated tokens; no byte setting by default | Runs and tool output                  | `modelContext.toolOutput.maxTokens` and optional `maxBytes` in `schemas.ts`; projection in `packages/agent-runtime/src/model-context-projection.ts`.           | The model receives the head and tail plus a bounding notice. Full output stays in history. These are projection targets, not strict byte ceilings.             |
| Simultaneous active runs in one conversation                    | 1                                                   | Conversations and runs                | Fixed in `packages/chat-server/src/conversations/run-start-workflow.ts` and `packages/postgres-store/src/postgres-agent-run-operations.ts`.                    | Another message is refused while the conversation has an active run.                                                                                           |
| Durable run observations read per poll                          | 100 every 500 ms                                    | Runs and observation events           | TypeScript options `observationBatchSize` and `pollIntervalMs` in `packages/agent-runtime/src/store-backed-agent-runtime.ts`; no release config knob.          | Events beyond a batch arrive on later polls.                                                                                                                   |
| Recent conversations in the conversation palette                | 8                                                   | Conversations per person              | Fixed `PALETTE_RECENT_LIMIT` in `packages/chat-ui/src/workspace/conversation-palette.tsx`.                                                                     | Only eight recent choices appear before searching. This does not cap the sidebar or storage.                                                                   |
| Conversation search results                                     | 20                                                  | Conversations per person or workspace | Fixed `CONVERSATION_SEARCH_RESULTS` in `packages/chat-ui/src/api/conversation-search-query.ts`.                                                                | Search shows the most recently changed matches. A narrower search finds other matches.                                                                         |
| Source text and model time for a generated title                | 800 characters; 60 seconds                          | New conversations                     | `MAX_TITLE_SOURCE_CHARS` (`conversation-title.ts`), `CONVERSATION_TITLE_TIMEOUT_MS` (`conversations/conversation-workflow.ts`) in `packages/chat-server/src`.  | Source text is shortened. A title call that times out leaves the existing title and follows the title job's retry policy.                                      |
| Result retained for replay of a changing operation              | 256 KiB                                             | Operation runs and result size        | Fixed `OPERATION_RUN_OUTPUT_MAX_BYTES` in `packages/tool-execution/src/operation-execution.ts`.                                                                      | The original call can succeed. Repeating it with the same key returns `409 OUTPUT_NOT_RETAINED` if its result was too large to keep. A call whose result holds a secret, such as a new API key, keeps no result at any size and answers the same.                           |

A data tool is an agent tool that exists as data, such as an operation of a Connection (`connection.<name>.<operation>`). It is called as an operation like every other tool, so the same policy applies: a changing data tool is refused for an agent under the default `confirm`, and it runs without a confirmation where an administrator's central setting says `allow`.

The conversation list uses the shared API paging defaults of 50 items, at most 200 per request (`listQuerySchema` in `packages/api-contract/src/shared.ts`). The sidebar asks for 30 conversations at a time (`RAIL_PAGE_SIZE` in `packages/chat-ui/src/api/rail-conversations.ts`): one request when a workspace opens, and one more each time a person scrolls to the end of the list or picks "Load more". The browser holds the pages a person has loaded until they switch workspace, so the rows held are 30 times the pages loaded, and every loaded row is on the page. While a run is active outside the open conversation, or a new conversation waits for its title, the sidebar reads its first page again every 2 seconds (`RAIL_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS` in `packages/chat-ui/src/workspace/use-conversation-list-refresh.ts`); no request reads more than one page.

When web fetching is enabled, tool calls also use the following budgets from `webAccess.fetch` in `packages/config-schema/src/schemas.ts`. Enforcement is in `packages/web-access/src/direct-web-fetcher.ts`.

| What it bounds                                     | Default                                                                                | Grows with                 | Knob and source                                          | What a person sees at the limit                                                 |
| -------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| One web fetch's time                               | 10 seconds; configured maximum 30 seconds                                              | Web fetches in runs        | `webAccess.fetch.timeoutMs`.                             | The tool returns a `timed_out` failure.                                         |
| Response bytes read and text returned from a fetch | 1 MiB response; 20,000 text characters; configured maxima 5 MiB and 200,000 characters | Web content loaded in runs | `webAccess.fetch.maxResponseBytes`, `maxTextCharacters`. | Returned content is shortened and marked `truncated`.                           |
| Redirects in one fetch                             | 5; configured maximum 10                                                               | Web fetches in runs        | `webAccess.fetch.maxRedirects`.                          | Too many redirects returns a `handler_failed` result naming the redirect limit. |

## Jobs and workers

Agent runs have their own worker and lease path when the assembly selects `agentRuntimeMode: "worker"`. `createClientInstanceApp` in `packages/client-assembly/src/app.ts` defaults to local execution in the API process, so the agent worker slot limit does not apply to that mode. Other background work uses the shared Postgres job executor. Worker slots are per process. Job kind concurrency limits apply across the instance.

| What it bounds                                                | Default                                                                                               | Grows with                                          | Knob and source                                                                                                                                                                                            | What a person sees at the limit                                                                                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Agent runs executing in one worker process                    | 1                                                                                                     | Simultaneous runs                                   | `AGENT_RUN_WORKER_CONCURRENCY`, read in `packages/client-assembly/src/agent-run-worker.ts`; fallback in `packages/agent-runtime/src/agent-run-worker.ts`.                                                  | Further runs stay queued until a slot is free.                                                                                                                                     |
| Agent run lease and heartbeat                                 | 10 minutes; heartbeat every 5 seconds                                                                 | Active runs                                         | `DEFAULT_LEASE_DURATION_MS`, `DEFAULT_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS` in `agent-run-worker.ts`; TypeScript options `leaseDurationMs`, `heartbeatIntervalMs`, no release config or environment knob.                 | A run whose worker loses its lease is reported as interrupted, rather than silently executed again.                                                                                |
| Connection discoveries running at the same time | 4 across the instance, 2 per API process, one per Connection; 6 attempts with waits from 15 seconds up to 5 minutes; a 3-minute lease | Connections that read their operations from their outside system, once per start of the API | Fixed `CONNECTION_DISCOVERY_MAX_RUNNING`, `CONNECTION_DISCOVERY_SLOTS`, `CONNECTION_DISCOVERY_MAX_ATTEMPTS` and the job kind `connection.discover` in `packages/chat-server/src/connection-jobs.ts`. | Further discoveries wait in the job queue. A Connection has at most two discoveries in the queue, the one that runs and one behind it, which is queued when the Connection changed while it was read or the API started meanwhile. Until its discovery ran, a newly accepted operation shows as awaiting discovery and no agent is given it. After the last attempt the job is dead: an operator retries it under Jobs, or the next start queues a new one. |
| One Connection discovery | 60 seconds; 500 operations; 4 MiB of operations as the JSON they are stored as; a description is cut at 4,000 characters; each schema within the bounds of the JSON Schema check | The answer of the outside system | Fixed `CONNECTION_DISCOVERY_TIMEOUT_MS`, `CONNECTION_DISCOVERY_MAX_OPERATIONS`, `CONNECTION_DISCOVERY_MAX_BYTES`, `CONNECTION_DISCOVERY_DESCRIPTION_MAX_CHARS` in `packages/connections/src/discovery.ts`; the schema bounds in `packages/connections/src/json-schema.ts`. | A discovery over the time, the count or the size fails, the Connection shows the error code, and the catalog stored before stays, so accepted operations go on working. An operation whose schema cannot be checked is left out and shows as unknown. So is an operation whose name, description or schema holds the Connection's credential: the Connection then shows the code `output_rejected`, and the audit timeline shows that discovery as a warning with the count and nothing of the operation. |
| Agent worker polling, cancellation checks and stale recovery  | Poll and cancellation every 1 second; recovery every 30 seconds, at most 50 runs per pass             | Queued, cancelled and lost runs                     | `DEFAULT_POLL_INTERVAL_MS`, `DEFAULT_CANCELLATION_POLL_INTERVAL_MS`, `DEFAULT_STALE_RECOVERY_INTERVAL_MS`, `DEFAULT_STALE_RECOVERY_LIMIT` in `agent-run-worker.ts`; corresponding TypeScript options only. | Queued work and cancellations wait for a check; excess stale runs wait for another recovery pass.                                                                                  |
| Agent worker shutdown drain                                   | 15 minutes                                                                                            | Active runs at shutdown                             | `AGENT_RUN_WORKER_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS`; `DEFAULT_AGENT_RUN_WORKER_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS` in `packages/client-assembly/src/agent-run-worker.ts`.                                                                    | Runs still active after the drain are interrupted. A second shutdown signal interrupts immediately.                                                                                |
| API recovery of stale active runs                             | 30 minutes stale; 50 candidates per pass; scheduled every minute                                      | Lost runs                                           | `DEFAULT_STALE_ACTIVE_RUN_MS`, `DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE` in `packages/chat-server/src/run-recovery.ts`; TypeScript `RunRecoveryOptions` only. Schedule in `packages/chat-server/src/job-kinds.ts`.              | Lost local runs become failed, allowing another message. Live worker runs use their leases. Startup recovery of local runs reads successive batches.                               |
| Title jobs                                                    | 4 global and 4 API slots; 1 per conversation; 2 attempts, 30 seconds between attempts; 2-minute lease | New conversations                                   | Fixed `generateConversationTitleJob` in `packages/chat-server/src/job-kinds.ts`; slots in `packages/chat-server/src/jobs.ts`.                                                                              | Titles wait in the queue. Exhausted attempts leave a dead job and the existing conversation title.                                                                                 |
| Account and workspace deletion jobs, separately per kind      | 4 global; 2 API slots; 1 per subject; 50 attempts; backoff from 1 minute to 6 hours; 10-minute lease  | People, workspaces and their conversations          | Fixed `deletionKind`, `DELETION_MAX_ATTEMPTS`, `DELETION_BACKOFF_BASE_MS`, `DELETION_BACKOFF_MAX_MS` in `job-kinds.ts`; `DELETION_SLOTS` in `jobs.ts`.                                                     | Deletion stays pending while cleanup retries. At exhaustion the job is dead and the subject stays closed.                                                                          |
| Scheduled API jobs                                            | 1 global and 1 API slot per kind; 1 attempt; normally a 10-minute lease                               | Conversations, audit events, usage and cleanup work | Fixed `defineScheduledKind` in `job-kinds.ts` and handlers in `jobs.ts`. Recovery and legacy adoption use 2-minute leases.                                                                                 | Work waits for the previous tick. A failed tick is visible in Jobs; the next tick does the next scheduled pass.                                                                    |
| Shared executor polling, scheduling checks and shutdown grace | Poll every 1 second; schedule check every 60 seconds; 20-second stop grace                            | Jobs across served kinds                            | Fixed `POLL_INTERVAL_MS`, `SCHEDULE_CHECK_INTERVAL_MS`, `STOP_GRACE_MS` in `packages/postgres-store/src/jobs/worker.ts`. Default heartbeat is lease duration divided by `HEARTBEATS_PER_LEASE` (3).        | Work waits for a poll. On shutdown unfinished jobs are released; expired leases are recovered according to the kind's attempt policy.                                              |
| Exhausted jobs handled in one batch                           | 20                                                                                                    | Failed jobs                                         | Fixed `EXHAUSTED_BATCH_SIZE` in `packages/postgres-store/src/jobs/store.ts`.                                                                                                                               | Further exhausted jobs wait for another pass before becoming dead or failed.                                                                                                       |
| Ended job record retention                                    | 7 days for succeeded or cancelled; 30 days for failed or dead                                         | Jobs                                                | Fixed `COMPLETED_JOB_RETENTION_DAYS`, `FAILED_JOB_RETENTION_DAYS` in `jobs/store.ts`; daily `pruneJobsSchedule` in `job-kinds.ts`.                                                                         | Older ended jobs disappear after pruning, except dead jobs for subjects still marked for deletion. Those remain until the subject is gone. Queued and running jobs are not pruned. |
| Jobs list response and refresh                                | 50 items by default, maximum 200; refresh every 10 seconds                                            | Jobs                                                | API `limit` in `listQuerySchema`, `packages/api-contract/src/shared.ts`; fixed `JOBS_REFRESH_MS` in `packages/chat-ui/src/settings/pages/jobs.tsx`.                                                        | Jobs loads another page on demand. A change may wait until the next refresh.                                                                                                       |
| Legacy preview and attachment adoption after an upgrade       | 500 rows per kind per tick, every minute                                                              | Assets and uploads awaiting jobs                    | Fixed `LEGACY_ADOPTION_BATCH_SIZE` in `packages/chat-server/src/jobs.ts`; `adoptLegacyJobsSchedule` in `job-kinds.ts`.                                                                                     | A large upgrade backlog is given jobs over several ticks.                                                                                                                          |
| Legacy workspace command adoption                             | 500 per tick, every 15 seconds                                                                        | Queued workspace commands from an earlier release   | Fixed `LEGACY_ADOPTION_BATCH_SIZE` in `packages/tool-execution/src/workspace-command-worker.ts`; `WORKSPACE_COMMAND_ADOPTION_INTERVAL_MS` in `packages/tool-execution/src/workspace-command-kind.ts`.      | Commands without jobs wait for adoption before execution.                                                                                                                          |
| Deletion cleanup and usage attribution batches                | 100 conversations per cleanup batch; 5,000 usage records per statement; pending count capped at 1,000 | People, conversations and model calls               | Fixed `PENDING_CLEANUP_BATCH_SIZE`, `USAGE_ATTRIBUTION_CLEAR_BATCH`, `STALLED_PENDING_COUNT_LIMIT` in `packages/chat-server/src/subject-deletion.ts`.                                                      | Cleanup continues in batches while successful. A stalled deletion stays pending; its reported pending count is capped, not its total cleanup work.                                 |
| Page builds in one worker process                             | 2; one per conversation                                                                               | Simultaneous saves of Pages                         | `PAGE_BUILD_CONCURRENCY`, read in `packages/client-assembly/src/pages.ts`; `JOB_UNCLAIMED_MS` in `packages/core/src/jobs.ts`; `PAGE_BUILD_WAIT_MS` in `chat-server/src/page-jobs.ts`.                                   | Further builds stay queued. A save fails after 30 seconds without any worker, after five minutes otherwise.                                                                        |
| One Page build                                                | 60 seconds; 500 output files, 50 MiB; 500 input files, 25 MiB; memory and CPU of the sandbox          | Size of the Page                                    | `PAGE_BUILD_TIMEOUT_MS`; `PAGE_BUILD_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES`, `PAGE_BUILD_MAX_OUTPUT_FILES` in `packages/app-build/src/limits.ts`; file set limits in `packages/core/src/pages.ts`; `infrastructure.sandbox`.    | The container is removed and the save fails with the reason; nothing is stored.                                                                                                    |

## Model usage and admission

Usage safeguards are instance totals across people, API processes and workers. Titles and guardrail checks also consume them. Admission reserves capacity before calling the provider. These safeguards can be exceeded when a completed call uses more than its reservation; they are not provider output caps.

| What it bounds                                             | Default                                                                                                                                                 | Grows with                                   | Knob and source                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | What a person sees at the limit                                                                                                                                      |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Model calls per UTC day                                    | Unset                                                                                                                                                   | People and model calls across runs           | `usage.safeguards.modelCallsPerDay` in `packages/config-schema/src/schemas.ts`; admission in `packages/usage-governance/src/index.ts`.                                                                                                                                                 | A new call is refused with a daily model call safeguard message.                                                                                                     |
| Tokens per UTC day and calendar month                      | Both unset                                                                                                                                              | Runs, conversation context and output        | `usage.safeguards.tokensPerDay`, `tokensPerMonth` in `schemas.ts`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | A new reservation that does not fit is refused. Limits at or below 16,000 are rejected during config validation.                                                     |
| Customer billable spend per day and month                  | Both unset; safety multiplier 1                                                                                                                         | Model calls and their token costs            | `usage.budget.dailySpendLimit`, `monthlySpendLimit`, `costSafetyMultiplier` in `schemas.ts`.                                                                                                                                                                                           | New calls are refused when a reservation does not fit. A model without a rate-card price is refused when a spend budget is configured. Usage shows the budget state. |
| Tokens reserved at admission                               | Input characters divided by 3, rounded up, plus 16,000 output tokens unless the request states a maximum                                                | Concurrent calls and context size            | Fixed `RESERVED_CHARACTERS_PER_INPUT_TOKEN` in `packages/usage-governance/src/index.ts`; `MODEL_CALL_RESERVED_OUTPUT_TOKENS` in `packages/core/src/usage.ts`.                                                                                                                          | A call can be refused before measured usage reaches the safeguard. Reservations are replaced by actual usage at settlement.                                          |
| Age of a pending call before abandoned-call recovery       | 6 hours; batches of 200, checked every 10 minutes                                                                                                       | Model calls lost with a process              | `USAGE_ABANDONED_AFTER_MS`, fixed `USAGE_RECOVERY_BATCH` in `usage-governance/src/index.ts`; TypeScript `abandonedAfterMs` only. Schedule in `packages/chat-server/src/job-kinds.ts`.                                                                                                  | Usage changes from Running to Abandoned and releases the reservation. Recovery reads further batches until finished.                                                 |
| Estimated usage when a broken stream has no provider usage | 10,000,000 input tokens and 10,000,000 output tokens; 1,000 web searches per call                                                                       | Interrupted calls and output size            | Fixed `MAX_ESTIMATED_TOKENS_PER_CALL`, `MAX_ESTIMATED_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_CALL` in `packages/model-provider/src/gateway.ts`.                                                                                                                                                              | Usage is marked Estimated. These cap accounting estimates, not the provider's actual work.                                                                           |
| Usage summary history and recent call list                 | 30 daily buckets; 25 recent events                                                                                                                      | Model calls                                  | Fixed `DAILY_USAGE_BUCKET_COUNT`, `RECENT_EVENT_COUNT` in `usage-governance/src/index.ts`.                                                                                                                                                                                             | The summary shows this window and recent sample. Older records remain stored.                                                                                        |
| Attribution backfill transactions                          | 5,000 usage events per batch                                                                                                                            | Older model calls                            | Fixed `USAGE_BACKFILL_BATCH` in `packages/chat-server/src/usage-backfill.ts`.                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Older attribution fills over successive transactions; interrupted work resumes from its checkpoint.                                                                  |
| Idle time in an OpenAI-compatible or Bedrock stream                   | 10 minutes without data                                                                                                                                 | Active model calls                           | Fixed `MODEL_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS` in `packages/model-provider/src/openai-compatible-stream.ts`.                                                                                                                                                                                     | The call fails with a timeout when the provider sends no data for that interval. This is not a total run deadline.                                                   |
| Provider retries before any unsafe replay                  | Transient retry waits of 1 and 4 seconds, with 20% jitter; at most 60 seconds total rate-limit waiting; non-rate-limit `Retry-After` at most 60 seconds | Concurrent model calls and provider failures | Fixed `MODEL_PROVIDER_RETRY_WAITS_MS`, `MODEL_PROVIDER_RETRY_JITTER_RATIO`, `MODEL_PROVIDER_RATE_LIMIT_WAIT_TOTAL_MS`, `MODEL_PROVIDER_RETRY_AFTER_MAX_MS` in `packages/model-provider/src/retry.ts`. `MODEL_PROVIDER_RATE_LIMIT_FIRST_WAIT_MS` is 4 seconds, doubled for later waits. | The call waits when replay is safe, then fails. A rate-limit failure says the model is receiving too many requests and to try again in a minute.                     |

Admission updates database counters atomically. API request rate counters are held in process memory, so the current deployment contract calls for one API process. Adding workers does not multiply the instance usage allowance, but a second API process would have separate request rate counters.

| What it bounds                                                         | Default                                                     | Grows with                                                           | Knob and source                                                                                                         | What a person sees at the limit                                                                                     |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| API calls to one operation per signed-in person or service, per minute | 6,000 reads; 1,200 writes; limiting enabled                 | People and requests per operation                                    | `rateLimits.enabled`, `readPerMinute`, `writePerMinute` in `packages/config-schema/src/schemas.ts`.                     | `429 RATE_LIMITED` with a `Retry-After` header and seconds to wait.                                                 |
| Sign-in or password attempts per minute                                | 10 per account and address; 300 per address across accounts | People sharing an address                                            | `rateLimits.signInPerAccountPerMinute`, `signInPerAddressPerMinute` in `schemas.ts`.                                    | `429 RATE_LIMITED`; a shared outer proxy address can make people share the address limit.                           |
| Refused credentials per address per minute                             | 60                                                          | Credential attempts                                                  | Fixed `REFUSED_CREDENTIALS_PER_ADDRESS_PER_MINUTE` in `packages/chat-server/src/http/rate-limit.ts`.                    | Refused credentials receive `429 RATE_LIMITED`; accepted credentials are unaffected by this counter.                |
| Dedicated in-memory rate counters                                      | 200,000, swept every minute                                 | Active people multiplied by operations called, plus address counters | `MAX_COUNTERS`, `SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS` in `http/rate-limit.ts`; TypeScript `createInProcessRateLimiter({ maxKeys })` only. | New callers share overflow counters once full and can receive 429 together. Existing callers retain their counters. |

## Assets and Studio

Studio reads a list page by page from `assets.list` and one asset from `assets.get` when its page opens (`packages/chat-ui/src/build-area/build-data.ts`). Search and the Namespace filter are answered by the instance. The browser holds the pages a person asked for, never the whole set. The overview and the export are still read by the CLI and by **Instance > Access**.

| What it bounds                                            | Default                                                                                                           | Grows with                  | Knob and source                                                                                                                                    | What a person sees at the limit                                                                                                  |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Rows read per Studio list request                          | 50                                                                                                                | Assets                      | Fixed `BUILD_LIST_PAGE_SIZE` in `packages/chat-ui/src/build-area/build-data.ts`.                                                                   | **Show more** reads the next page. Nothing beyond the pages asked for is fetched.                                                |
| Skills offered in an agent's skill picker                 | 50 per search                                                                                                     | Skills                      | Fixed `SKILL_CHOICE_PAGE_SIZE` in `packages/chat-ui/src/build-area/agent-kind.tsx`.                                                                | A skill outside the first 50 is found by typing part of its name.                                                                |
| Revisions read when History opens                         | 50 per page, newest first                                                                                         | Revisions of one asset      | Fixed `BUILD_HISTORY_PAGE_SIZE` in `packages/chat-ui/src/build-area/build-data.ts`.                                                                | **Show more** reads the next page. A restore reads the one revision it restores.                                                 |
| Asset revision list response                              | 50, maximum 200                                                                                                   | Revisions of assets         | API `limit` in `listQuerySchema`, `packages/api-contract/src/shared.ts`; route in `packages/chat-server/src/routes/asset-routes.ts`.               | Another cursor page is needed for older revisions.                                                                               |
| Agent-proposed skill change text and resulting skill size | 20,000 characters per operation text; 60,000 characters in the root and separately in each resource; 30 resources | Skills and proposed changes | Fixed `SKILL_CHANGE_MAX_OPERATION_TEXT`, `SKILL_CHANGE_MAX_CONTENT`, `SKILL_CHANGE_MAX_RESOURCES` in `packages/config-schema/src/skill-change.ts`. | Invalid or oversized proposed changes are rejected. These are proposal limits, not a general cap on all assets edited or synced. |
| Files in one write of an App | 8 MiB decoded in one call; 500 files, 2 MiB per file and 25 MiB per stored file set | Size of the App | Fixed `ASSET_PUT_FILES_MAX_BYTES`, `FILE_SET_MAX_FILES`, `FILE_SET_MAX_FILE_BYTES`, `FILE_SET_MAX_TOTAL_BYTES` in `packages/core/src/pages.ts`; the route's body limit `ASSET_PUT_BODY_LIMIT_BYTES` in `packages/chat-server/src/asset-files.ts`. `platform.context.get` reports the four limits with the kind. A reverse proxy in front of the instance must let a body of 12 MiB through. | The write is refused with `VALIDATION_FAILED` naming the constant. Nothing is stored. |
| Files in one read of an App revision | 8 MiB of source files in one answer; 8 object reads at a time | Size of the App; not the number of its revisions | Fixed `ASSET_GET_FILES_MAX_BYTES` in `packages/core/src/pages.ts`, reported by `platform.context.get`; `ASSET_GET_FILE_READS_IN_FLIGHT` in `packages/chat-server/src/asset-files.ts`. Per read: one read of the asset, one of the revision by its number, one of the file set, and one object read per file. | A set above the limit, such as an App saved from a larger Page, is answered as its index with `filesOmitted: true` and without contents; no object is read. |
| A write of an App waiting for its build | 60 seconds; one build job per write | Simultaneous writes of Apps and saves of Pages, which share the build workers | Fixed `APP_BUILD_WAIT_MS` in `packages/chat-server/src/page-jobs.ts`; the workers are sized by `PAGE_BUILD_CONCURRENCY`. | The write answers `504 TIMEOUT` with `build_timeout`, its job is withdrawn and no revision and no file set exist. The caller sends the write again. |
| Listing Apps for a member | One page of `assets.list`: the reads of any asset list (the keys of the page in batches, then the assets of the page with their draft and published revision in one read). The published title comes with that read; a member's list costs no further request | Apps in the workspace; a member whose workspace holds many unpublished Apps scans more keys per page | Fixed `DEFAULT_ASSET_LIST_LIMIT` in `packages/chat-server/src/asset-workflow.ts` and `ASSET_LIST_SCAN_BATCH` in `packages/postgres-store`. | Further Apps are on the next page. |
| Opening a published App | Per address: one read of the asset with its published pointer and one of the file set, signing only. Past 20,000 addresses in one process, each further file request asks the rights again and is slower, not refused. |

A config push is one `assets.sync` call: at most 2,000 items for a holder of the release right and 200 for every other caller (`ASSET_RELEASE_SYNC_MAX_ITEMS`, `ASSET_SYNC_MAX_ITEMS` in `packages/api-contract/src/assets.ts`), in a request body of at most 20 MiB (`ASSET_SYNC_BODY_MAX_BYTES`, the same file), of which one put item takes at most 2 MiB (`ASSET_SYNC_ITEM_MAX_BYTES`). All four are fixed. The body is parsed in memory before any check, so one push costs up to that much memory and blocks the process while it is parsed; the write rate limit bounds how many arrive. A push takes one lock per instance on the asset set, so pushes and saves of one instance are applied one after another, each for the time of its own items. Under the lock the statements grow with the items in steps of 500 (`ASSET_WRITE_CHUNK` in `packages/postgres-store/src/postgres-config-asset-operations.ts`), not per item: the rows of all named assets in one read, their highest revisions in one, then inserts and one update per 500 items. Measured on a local Postgres 17 with small skills: 200 updates in 7 statements and about 40 ms, 2,000 creates in 12 statements and about 200 ms, 2,000 updates in 13 statements and about 170 ms. Larger definitions add transfer time, bounded by the 20 MiB body. Before the write the lock also covers one read of the active revision ids of the instance (one row per active asset), and a full read of the asset set only when another write changed it since this one was checked. The CLI says to push in parts with `--only` at either limit. A first `catalyst config pull` reads each asset with one `assets.get`, eight at a time, so it grows with the asset count and is bounded by `rateLimits.readPerMinute` (default 6,000); later pulls read only assets whose revision changed. No total asset-count ceiling exists; that gap is listed below.

| Audit event retention                           | 365 days; maximum configured value 3,650; pruned daily | People and audited activity                        | `retention.auditDays` in `config-schema/src/schemas.ts`; `pruneAuditEventsSchedule` in `chat-server/src/job-kinds.ts`.                                                                                               | Events older than the cutoff disappear; an `audit.pruned` event records the count.                                    |
| Curated audit activity view                     | Fetch 500 raw events, show at most 100 activities      | Audit events                                       | Fixed `AUDIT_EVENT_FETCH_LIMIT`, `AUDIT_ACTIVITY_LIMIT` in `packages/chat-server/src/routes/audit-routes.ts`.                                                                                                        | Only recent grouped activities appear. The raw audit feed uses cursor paging.                                         |

For data sources declared under `dataSources`, `packages/config-schema/src/schemas.ts` defaults `sql.statementTimeoutMs` to 10,000 and `sql.maxRows` to 5,000, with a configured maximum of 50,000 rows. `packages/data-source/src/index.ts` applies the timeout and slices the fetched result, marking it `truncated`. The row setting therefore bounds the returned result, not all rows already fetched into memory.

The separate `@vivd-catalyst/postgres-connector` executor enforces the following ceilings. Its source is `packages/postgres-connector/src/executor/limits.ts`. `PostgresLimits` is a TypeScript target option, not a release config key, and can only lower the four stated limits.

| What it bounds                                           | Default                                                                        | Grows with                 | Knob and source                                                                                                                                                                       | What a person sees at the limit                                                                                         |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Connections to one target under one credential           | 4                                                                              | Concurrent query runs      | `POSTGRES_POOL_MAX_CONNECTIONS`; lower with `PostgresLimits.maxConnections`.                                                                                                          | A query waits for a connection.                                                                                         |
| Wait for a connector connection                          | 5 seconds                                                                      | Concurrent query runs      | Fixed `POSTGRES_POOL_ACQUIRE_WAIT_MS`.                                                                                                                                                | The executor returns a `busy` failure when no connection becomes free. This is a wait deadline, not a queue length cap. |
| Query execution time                                     | 15 seconds, plus 1 second for the executor's cancellation deadline             | Query work                 | `POSTGRES_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS`; lower with `PostgresLimits.statementTimeoutMs`. Fixed `POSTGRES_DEADLINE_GRACE_MS`; cancellation repeats every `POSTGRES_CANCEL_REPEAT_MS` (100 ms). | A timed-out query fails and is cancelled.                                                                               |
| Returned rows and bytes                                  | 1,000 rows; 2 MiB                                                              | Query result size          | `POSTGRES_RESULT_MAX_ROWS`, `POSTGRES_RESULT_MAX_BYTES`; lower with `PostgresLimits.maxRows`, `maxBytes`.                                                                             | The result reports `truncatedBy: rows` or `bytes`.                                                                      |
| Cursor fetch batch and socket read margin                | 100 rows per batch; 16 MiB beyond the result byte cap                          | Rows and large values      | Fixed `POSTGRES_CURSOR_BATCH_ROWS`, `POSTGRES_READ_MARGIN_BYTES`.                                                                                                                     | Caps are checked after batches. A read far beyond the byte cap can end the connection before the value is fully read.   |
| Query input                                              | 20,000 characters; 100 parameters                                              | Query text and parameters  | Fixed `POSTGRES_QUERY_TEXT_MAX_CHARS`, `POSTGRES_PARAMETERS_MAX_COUNT`.                                                                                                               | Oversized input is rejected before execution.                                                                           |
| Privilege objects listed in a probe                      | 200                                                                            | Connected database objects | Fixed `POSTGRES_PRIVILEGE_OBJECTS_MAX_LISTED`.                                                                                                                                        | The probe lists a bounded sample of objects.                                                                            |
| Connector connection startup, idle close and replacement | 30-second connect timeout; 60-second idle close; 2,700-second maximum lifetime | Connections                | Fixed `POSTGRES_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, `POSTGRES_POOL_IDLE_CLOSE_SECONDS`, `POSTGRES_CONNECTION_MAX_LIFETIME_SECONDS`.                                                             | Connection startup can fail; idle or aged connections are replaced.                                                     |

## Not yet stated

These are gaps in the platform code searched for this page, not promises of unlimited capacity.

- **Chat and runs:** a maximum queued or simultaneously active run count across the instance, a per-person daily run quota, a hard total agent run duration, an enforced generic operation timeout, a total conversation or message ceiling, and a cap on the full recent conversation list loaded by the browser. The palette's eight choices and search's 20 matches do not provide those ceilings. Provider context windows depend on the selected model; no universal context ceiling is stated here.
- **Jobs and workers:** a maximum queued job count or a shared queue admission budget across kinds. Per-kind concurrency and per-process slots limit execution, not enqueueing.
- **Model usage and admission:** a default instance call, token or spend allowance, and a platform-wide simultaneous model call ceiling. The optional safeguards are unset by default. The 16,000-token reservation does not set a provider output maximum.
- **Assets and Studio:** a total asset count or byte ceiling, a ceiling on the full overview response, and revision retention. Studio itself no longer reads the overview.
- **Workspaces and files:** a total instance storage budget, a total workspace or membership count, a queue length ceiling for commands or browser uploads, and one upload budget covering every attachment handler. The workspace source file budget covers that handler only.
- **Documents:** a universal ingestion page, byte or document-count cap, an extraction queue limit, and document worker concurrency, leases or retention for capability-owned processing. The platform preview worker's limits do not establish them.
- **Inbox and approvals:** a total pending request ceiling, a cap on the complete Inbox fetch, retention for all approval requests, and a concurrency ceiling for the parallel guardrail check calls.
- **Database:** a platform database size or row ceiling, a platform query statement timeout, a platform connection acquisition deadline or queue length cap, a connector waiter-count cap, and a usage record retention period. Usage records remain after account or workspace deletion with attribution removed. Migration lock acquisition also has no deadline (`packages/postgres-store/src/migrations.ts`).

For generic operations, `DEFAULT_OPERATION_TIMEOUT_MS` in `packages/chat-server/src/operations/operation-face.ts` declares 300,000 ms (five minutes), overridable through the TypeScript binding's `timeoutMs`. The current `packages/tool-execution/src/run-operation.ts` calls the operation without consuming that timeout. No timeout message or enforced ceiling follows from the declaration alone.

For 5,000 to 10,000 people, record the expected peak active runs, model calls per run, documents and bytes per day, asset count, and retained conversation volume before assigning hardware. Validate those workloads against the instance's actual configuration and capability packages. This page supplies code limits; it supplies no measured throughput claim.

pages.title: Deployment
pages.description: Package and run a dedicated client instance.
pages.body:
Workshape Catalyst runtime services are packaged as Docker images. Docker Compose is the default local and first production-friendly deployment target.

## First Production Shape

```text
reverse proxy / TLS
  -> chat API service
  -> standalone or embedded chat frontend assets
  -> optional tool worker service
  -> Postgres
  -> object storage or backup target
  -> logs, metrics, backups, and deploy scripts
```

Caddy is the default reverse proxy/TLS choice for the first VPS or VM deployment because it keeps automatic HTTPS and routing simple.

The API limits how often one caller may call an operation, and counts a caller who is not
signed in by client address. It reads that address from `X-Forwarded-For` only when the request
comes from a loopback or private address, which is the reverse proxy on the Compose network.
Caddy as the outermost proxy passes the real client address without configuration.

Where another proxy or load balancer stands in front of Caddy (Traefik, a cloud load
balancer), Caddy must be told to trust it. Without this Caddy reports the outer proxy as the
client, and everyone who signs in shares one count:

```caddyfile
{
	servers {
		trusted_proxies static private_ranges
	}
}
```

Name the outer proxy's addresses instead of `private_ranges` where they are known. After the
change, sign in from two networks and check that the API's request log shows two different
`remoteAddress` values.

The counters live in the API process, so an instance runs exactly one API process. The numbers
are set in the release config, see [Rate limits](/configure/release-config/#rate-limits).

## Agent Runs

An Agent Run is a row and a job of the kind `agent_run.execute`. The API writes both in the
transaction that accepts the message and never executes a run itself. A job worker claims the
job, the job claims the run, and every event and message of the run is stored under the lease
of that job.

Where the worker runs is set in the client assembly with `agentRunWorker`:

- `"in_process"` (default): the API process serves the runs with a second job worker. Closing
  the API process ends its runs as interrupted at once.
- `"separate"`: only the processes started with `runAgentRunWorker` serve the runs. On SIGTERM
  such a process takes no new run and gives its runs `AGENT_RUN_WORKER_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS` to
  end, 15 minutes unless set. A second signal ends the drain. In Compose, set the worker's
  `stop_grace_period` to at least the drain timeout plus 30 seconds; with less, Docker kills
  the worker mid-drain and its runs fail as lost after the lease time.

One process executes `AGENT_RUN_WORKER_CONCURRENCY` runs at once, 8 unless set. The runs of an
instance that execute at once are that number times its worker processes; further runs wait
queued in the order they were accepted. Keep the default of 8 unless measured otherwise: a
worker process with 8 runs in progress was measured at 201 MB. A run is never executed twice:

- The worker of a run was killed: after the lease time of 90 seconds the next pass of any job
  worker of the instance, the API's included, fails the run with `AGENT_RUN_WORKER_LOST`, the
  reply is shown as interrupted and the conversation takes the next message. Until then the
  reply stands still. No worker has to come back for this.
- The worker was stopped and the run did not end within the drain time: the run fails with
  `AGENT_RUN_RUNTIME_INTERRUPTED`.
- A run stored no event for 30 minutes: it fails as interrupted.
- No Agent Run worker takes a run within 10 minutes of its acceptance: the run fails with
  `AGENT_RUN_NOT_STARTED`, the person is told that the reply could not be started, and the
  conversation takes the next message. The same happens when the backlog is longer than the
  workers take in that time, so add slots or processes before the wait of a healthy instance
  comes near it. Instance > Jobs marks `agent_run.execute` with "No worker takes these" when
  its jobs have been due for a minute and none is running.

A stop request reaches the worker within about a second. The answer of a run and the end of the
run are stored together, so a worker killed at the end of a run leaves no answer beside a
failed run.

Rolling back to the previous release in the single-process topology leaves the runs that were
in flight `running` for up to 30 minutes, with their conversations answering 409, until that
release's own recovery fails them.

## Page Builds

With the module `apps` on, the tool `page.save` stores a folder of a conversation's Execution Workspace as a revision of a Page. The build is the job kind `page.bundle`, and the workspace command worker serves it:

- The worker reads the files by the index the save recorded, checks size and checksum of each, and writes a copy into a temporary directory of its own under `WORKSPACE_COMMAND_TEMP_ROOT`. The directory is removed when the build ends.
- The build is the fixed command `catalyst-page-build` of the runner image, run in the sandbox like a workspace command: no network, read-only root file system, no capabilities, and the CPU, memory and process limits of `infrastructure.sandbox`. Only that directory is mounted. The command gets no environment variable of the worker.
- The worker treats what the command left behind as untrusted data. It reads regular files only, follows no link, refuses a path that leaves the directory or has a `__catalyst` segment, and stops at the file and byte limits instead of reading past them.
- No file of a Page is parsed or run in the API process or in a worker process.

An instance with `modules.apps.enabled: true` needs:

- `executionWorkspaces.enabled: true` and, outside development, `infrastructure.sandbox.provider: docker`. The instance does not start otherwise and names the setting.
- A running workspace command worker. It needs `infrastructure.objectStorage.files` and its credentials in addition to the workspace store. A worker that does not serve `page.bundle` does not start.
- A runner image of the same release. Both runner images carry the command: the platform's `workspace-command-runner` target and the runner image of the capabilities repository. Each runs `catalyst-page-build --check` when it is built, which builds a small Page, so an image without a working command does not come out of its build. An older image has no `catalyst-page-build`; every save then fails with a message that says the runner image must be rolled out. The Infrastructure page does not show this.

The same worker keeps the repositories of assets whose files are one, with two more job kinds:

- `asset_repo.commit` makes the commit of a save. The worker reads the bundles the ledger names from the `files` store, each to no more than the size the ledger recorded, and hands the command only a bundle whose SHA-256 is the recorded one; any other ends the save with `bundle_hash_mismatch`. The commit is the fixed command `catalyst-asset-repo` of the runner image, which runs git in the sandbox under the same limits as a build. The worker believes the result only when the bundle the command left has the size and the hash the result names. It names the bundle on the save's row before it puts the object.
- `asset_repo.sweep` runs every hour. It gives up the saves that did not finish within a day and removes their objects. The object store is never listed: an object is found by its row.

A commit keeps everything it works on below one directory on the disk of the worker, which is the only directory its container mounts: the files, the bundles of the repository, the command's repository and the new bundle. Nothing of it is in the `/tmp` of the sandbox, so a commit takes none of the container's memory for its files; the memory limit of the sandbox (4 GiB unless the instance sets another) holds git and the command, which read one file of at most 2 MiB at a time. One commit takes at most 550 MiB of disk (`ASSET_REPO_COMMIT_DISK_BYTES`: five times the 50 MiB a tree may have and three times the 100 MiB a history may have), two run at a time, and the directory is removed when the commit ended. The worker starts no commit on a disk with less room and refuses the save with `no_space`, as it does when the disk fills on the way; an operator frees space on the worker. A save reads every bundle of the repository. Together they may have 100 MiB (`ASSET_REPO_MAX_BUNDLE_BYTES`); a save that would leave more is refused with `history_too_large`.

Git is in the runner image alone. An older runner image has no `catalyst-asset-repo`; a save then fails with a message that says the runner image must be rolled out. On a `local` sandbox the command runs the git of the machine, which has to be 2.47 or later.

Neither a save nor a command waits for a worker that is not there. Every job worker reports every 10 seconds which kinds of job it claims. A `workspace.exec` call whose command has been due for 30 seconds while the workers of its kind reported nothing for 30 seconds fails: the agent reads that code execution is unavailable and tells the person, and the run goes on. A command behind a worker that reports waits.
